ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The principal AML/CFT statutes are the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 19058, last amended effective 25 March 2023), the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 17113), their Enforcement Decrees, and the Financial Services Commission identification and verification regulations; beneficial ownership of corporate entities is reported to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and other competent authorities through Foreign Exchange Transactions Act inward investment reporting and financial customer due diligence rules, and is not made publicly searchable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified true copy from corporate registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the issuing jurisdiction followed by one parallel mechanism only: if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an apostille from its competent authority; if the issuing state is not a party, obtain authentication from its foreign ministry and consular legalization from the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (functional equivalent for Korean entity: Certificate of Corporate Registration Extract and Certificate of No Tax Arrears)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court registry office / National Tax Service, Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Korean-issued certificates, apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; for foreign-issued certificates, notarization plus either apostille (Hague member state) or consular legalization (non-member state). No path combines the two.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the founding corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed original attested by the company secretary, notarized by a local notary, and then processed under the single applicable method: apostille by the competent authority of an Apostille member state or consular legalization through the ROK diplomatic mission in a non-member state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the proposed Chusik Hoesa (draft and finally executed copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders of the Korean entity and Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Articles executed before a Korean notary; for foreign legalization of the executed Korean articles, notarize and then apostille through the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs only. Consular legalization is not added to an apostilled document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution maintaining the founding shareholder's principal account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued on bank letterhead and signed by a branch officer, notarized by a local notary, then apostilled (Hague member) or consular legalized at the ROK embassy or consulate (non-member state). Use only one authentication path; never sequence apostille and consular legalization together.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Each UBO, director, executive officer, and authorised signatory must be screened before onboarding and continuously thereafter against: (i) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list; (ii) the United States OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, including primary and secondary sanctions; (iii) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) the Republic of Korea KoFIU and Financial Services Commission enforcement and sanctions lists; and (v) domestic Korean PEP registers covering prominent public officials. All PEPs, including foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates, require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth review, senior management approval, and enhanced monitoring for at least twelve months after public office ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea - Internet Registration Office (i-RO)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be written in Hangul in the articles of incorporation and registry files; a Latin/English parallel name may be registered for foreign commercial use. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive element, (2) a business-objective description, (3) the legal-form suffix Chusik Hoesa, and (4) an industry or activity descriptor. Hanja and Roman characters may be used as auxiliary readings, but the controlling transcription for foreign words is the National Institute of Korean Language's roman-to-Hangul transliteration rules; identical names and deceptively similar names within the same registration district are prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a written rejection notice stating the statutory reason. Within seven days the applicant may file a reconsideration request with the same district registration office using the prescribed form and cure any defective name element. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may file a formal objection within fourteen days to the district court having jurisdiction over the registration office; the court must decide the objection expeditiously. A further administrative appeal lies to the Seoul Administrative Court, and ultimately to the Supreme Court of Korea. A foreign applicant must act through Korean counsel holding a valid power of attorney, and should all deadlines be missed, may commence a new name search because the name-reservation window is non-extendable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: In Korea the registered office must be a real, fixed, physically identifiable address within the jurisdiction of the registry where judicial and tax notices can be served. A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox will generally satisfy neither the National Tax Service business registration criterion nor domestic bank account-opening due diligence. For the ISIC 6201 EdTech subscription business using Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the entity needs a verifiable operational site, a local tax presence, and access to its payment reconciliation records; a virtual mailbox may be used only as an auxiliary receiving point alongside a valid serviced-office lease, and even then local banks may reject it. The recommended practice is a dedicated serviced office or co-working space under a written lease with nameplate and physical presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspections may be performed by the National Tax Service, district tax office, municipal tax authorities, court officers, and KFIU supervisory examiners. Checklist for inspection: (1) executed lease agreement and proof of paid deposit or rent; (2) corporate nameplate and business registration certificate display; (3) actual workstations, computers, files and staffing; (4) accounting books, invoice records, and app-store settlement records; and (5) physical access for process servers. Quantified risk: dedicated serviced office with staff - low (10-15 percent); bare virtual office or mailbox - high (65-85 percent); residential address used as registered office without permitted home-office approval - high (75 percent).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean notary public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs; external consulate where applicable

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 288, 289, 291-295, 300, 317, 329, 330, 331, 332, 333, 363, 368, 382, 383, 385, 389, 393, 397, and 398; Framework Act on Registration of Real Estate, Companies, etc. and the Commercial Registration Rules of the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Court Registry Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office) under the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Corporate Establishment Registration Application for a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Chusik Hoesa under the amended Commercial Act. The incorporators may declare any capital amount above zero, but the issue price per share must be at least KRW 100. If capital is paid in cash, the full subscription price must be deposited into a restricted escrow account opened in the name of the company under formation at a licensed Korean bank, and a certificate of deposit must be obtained and submitted to the Court Registry Office. The escrow restriction remains in force until the company is registered and the court notifies the bank to release the funds; any withdrawal before completion is void. Non-cash contributions require independent valuation and will be scrutinized by the registry court.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY: The Board of Directors of the above-captioned Korean Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa), duly convened pursuant to Article 390 of the Commercial Act, in the presence of the directors elected at incorporation, unanimously adopts the following resolutions: 1. Adoption of Registered Office: The Board hereby adopts as the registered office and principal administrative address the place stated in the Articles of Incorporation, namely Unit 45, Floor 17, Teheran-ro 123, Gangnam-gu, Seoul 06142, Republic of Korea. The Chief Executive Officer is authorized to execute, renew, and terminate the lease for the registered office, to pay security deposits and rent from corporate funds, and to notify the Court Registry Office of any transfer of the registered office within the same city or to another jurisdiction as required by the Commercial Act. 2. Subscription and Confirmation of Share Capital: The Board ratifies the incorporation subscription of 20,000 fully paid common shares, each with a par value of KRW 5,000 and an aggregate paid-in capital of KRW 100,000,000. The Board confirms that the full subscription price has been lawfully deposited into a restricted escrow account at a licensed Korean bank before registration and that the capital has been distributed among the incorporators as set out in the subscription ledger. The Board declares that no share has been issued for less than par value and that all restrictions on withdrawal of escrowed funds are acknowledged. 3. Banking and Payment Authorization: The Board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly or severally, to open and maintain corporate bank accounts, including a dedicated operating account and a merchant account for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlements, with Kookmin Bank or Hana Bank. The officers are authorized to execute account agreements, electronic banking mandates, payment gateway agreements, and deposit and withdrawal documents, and to approve payments up to KRW 20,000,000 per transaction or KRW 100,000,000 per month without further board approval. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers: The Board appoints NAME A as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, NAME B as Standing Internal Director and Chief Operating Officer, NAME C as Internal Director and Chief Financial Officer, and NAME D as Auditor, who shall not concurrently hold an executive position prohibited by law. The Chief Executive Officer shall represent the Company in all domestic and foreign affairs and may delegate, by power of attorney, to other directors or employees. 5. Corporate Governance and Compliance: The Board directs management to complete the tax and business registration with the National Tax Service, to adopt internal accounting controls and anti-money-laundering policies, to issue share certificates, to maintain a registered shareholders ledger, and to submit to an annual financial statement audit if the Company exceeds the statutory thresholds. The Board approves the reimbursement of all incorporation expenses and orders the corporate secretary to file any required post-registration notices. 6. Closing: All resolutions were passed by the unanimous affirmative vote of the directors present; no director abstained. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of the first board meeting certified by the chairman and the auditor.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, review, and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Notarial Association and an authorized notary public in the Korean jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare articles of incorporation in Korean containing the trade name, object clauses covering software development, EdTech services, language-learning content and online subscription distribution, location of registered office, share capital, par value, number of authorized shares, amount paid in, method of public notice, and names of incorporators. The articles shall be signed by every incorporator before a notary public, who will verify identity and legal capacity, certify the Deed of Incorporation, and issue a notarized text. Submit the draft electronically or in person together with an identification card of each incorporator and the final draft of articles. Ensure that the objects include implementation of remote language-learning software and subscription services to avoid ultra vires concerns and to match the scope of ISIC 6201 and NAICS 611710.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identification card of each incorporator
Draft articles of incorporation in Korean
Power of attorney if an agent acts for an incorporator
Proof of reserved trade name
Certificate of address for the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary public queries the object clauses or the par value provisions, amend the articles to conform to Commercial Act formalities and submit a revised draft for re-notarization. If the notary refuses certification because of identity mismatch, provide corrected, notarized identification or a fresh passport copy and resubmit within the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of shares and deposit of paid-in capital into restricted escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank with a branch in the Republic of Korea (for example, Kookmin Bank or Hana Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit at least the aggregate subscription price of the issued shares in cash into an account titled Capital Deposit for Incorporation opened by the incorporators or a designated agent. Because there is no minimum capital requirement under Article 295 of the Commercial Act, the incorporators may deposit any declared amount; nevertheless, for financial credibility and tax filings, set paid-in capital at KRW 100,000,000. The bank must issue a certificate of deposit confirming that the capital is blocked and may not be withdrawn until the company is registered and the court notifies the bank of the release. Retain the original certificate for attachment to the incorporation application and deliver a copy to the corporate secretary.
required_dossiers: Stock subscription forms signed by each subscriber
Deposit remittance confirmation or bank transfer receipt
Identification documents of the incorporators or authorized agent
Bank account opening form for the escrow account
Draft articles of incorporation for the bank record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the escrow account or issue the certificate because of a mismatch in the name or passport number of a subscriber, correct the bank records by filing an amendment to the account opening form and return the deposit to the originating account. Then re-deposit the funds and obtain a new certificate before the registration filing deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration with the Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; if located in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office corresponding under the Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration within 14 days of the date of payment of the capital. Submit the application electronically through the Korean court electronic registration system or in person at the registry window, attaching the notarized articles, the bank certificate of capital deposit, the subscription ledger, the list of directors and auditor, the written consent of the officers accepting their positions, and the proof of payment of registration tax and court fees. The registry court will examine compliance with Articles 317 and 330 of the Commercial Act, verify the legality of the corporate governance structure, and, if satisfied, assign a corporate registration number and issue the certificate of incorporation. If a defect is found, the court will issue a correction order; the applicant must cure the defect within the prescribed period, usually 14 days, and resubmit without losing the original filing date.
required_dossiers: Notarized articles of incorporation
Original bank certificate of capital deposit
Subscription ledger and list of subscribers
List of initial directors and statutory auditor
Written acceptance of office signed by each officer
Proof of payment of registration tax and education surcharge
Corporate registration application form
Corporate seal (dojang) specimen and seal certificate application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry court issues a correction order for a technical deficiency, the authorized agent shall prepare a cure submission, pay any revised fees, and refile within the specified period. If the application is rejected, the incorporators may file a new application after correcting the grounds, or seek a formal review from the registration court with legal counsel; otherwise, the previous registration tax may be refunded and re-paid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration business tax registration, bank account activation, and adoption of corporate governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through Hometax online portal and the competent district tax office (Seoul Regional Tax Office or the district office of the registered address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of corporate registration, adopt the First Board Resolution and register the company with the National Tax Service for corporate income tax, business income tax, value-added tax, and withholding purposes; obtain the Business Registration Certificate by filing the prescribed application with the competent district tax office or through Hometax. Prepare the corporate seal, register the authorized directors, activate the corporate banking account using the certificate of incorporation and the seal certificate, and register for e-tax and e-invoice billing. For EdTech subscription services, no separate content license is required; however, if the company processes personal data of users, submit the required privacy policy and data-processing registration under the Personal Information Protection Act, and if selling digital content, ensure Apple IAP and Google Play Billing agreements are in place. The company should also open an escrow settlement account if required by app marketplace mandates.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Corporate seal (dojang) certificate
Copy of the registered office lease agreement
Identification of the representative director and directors
Application for business registration
Articles of incorporation and first board resolution minutes
Corporate bank account details
Personal data processing policy for the EdTech service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business classification, provide the corporate registration certificate, the customer subscription agreements, and an ISIC 6201 and NAICS 611710 mapping narrative to support the software and education-service classification. If the business registration certificate is suspended or delayed because of missing address documentation, submit a certified copy of the lease and a clean building usage certificate within seven days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for a pure digital EdTech and computer programming service; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation is conducted under ISIC 6201, and no industrial licensing board approval is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable (no statutory operating permit is required for software development, online language tutoring, or subscription-based EdTech services beyond the general business registration with the National Tax Service).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (the activity involves no physical facility, wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, hazardous waste generation, or installation falling within the Environmental Impact Assessment Act or its subordinate tiers).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the company shall nevertheless ensure that any future move into a leased commercial office complies with indoor air quality and building hygiene standards under the Indoor Air Quality Control Act, but no industrial EIA threshold arises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for an industrial fire permit; however, the registered office and any commercial lease must comply with the Fire Services Act (Act No. 4260, as amended), requiring basic fire-extinguishing equipment, a fire evacuation plan, and, where necessary, a certificate of completion of fire-fighting systems from the National Fire Agency and local fire station. Workplace safety in an office environment is governed by the Occupational Safety and Health Act, and, if the company hires five or more full-time employees, a workplace safety and health manager appointment is mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (Hometax) at https://www.hometax.go.kr; export clearance and customs proof are processed through the Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic place of business must first appoint a tax representative in Korea, then file a business registration application under the Value-Added Tax Act. The delegate must submit: certified copies of the foreign certificate of incorporation, board resolution appointing the representative, power of attorney, proof of the entity's registered address, evidence of the taxable activity or place of supply in Korea, and any Korean bank account evidence. The application is submitted to the NTS district tax office or through HomeTax using the statutory business registration form. After verification the NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the TIN and VAT ID for all subsequent filings; ongoing compliance including filing and payment may be performed by the tax representative under the Korean tax law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; the Republic of Korea does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0; registration is mandatory for every business operator with taxable supplies in Korea; a Chusik Hoesa corporation does not benefit from any turnover-based VAT registration exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) are mandatory for all business-to-business supplies and must be transmitted through HomeTax to the NTS by the day after issuance; the HomeTax system performs digital validation and assigns an electronic seal/barcode for anti-fraud control. The fiscal clearance model is near-real-time transmission, not Latin American pre-clearance blocking; paper tax invoices and cash receipts are also monitored for B2C supplies. Failure to issue or transmit, or late transmission, is subject to statutory surcharges and late-filing penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods qualify for 0% VAT when removed from Korea under a customs export declaration. Export services and offshore digital services, including EdTech subscription and language-learning content delivered to non-resident customers outside Korea, are zero-rated when the place of supply is outside Korea and the supplier holds credible evidence of non-resident status and foreign actual consumption. Nothing impairs the right to input VAT credit/refund; the claim must be substantiated on the periodic VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS evidencing the export and the FOB value
Ocean Bill of Lading, Airwaybill, or multimodal transport document showing physical departure from Korea for exported goods
Commercial invoice, packing list, and sales contract matching the export declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Korean bank credit advice proving the export proceeds were received in foreign currency
For zero-rated services: signed contract, delivery/usage logs, IP address or geolocation evidence of the overseas recipient, and non-resident status certificate/passport data
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS cross-validates zero-rated export claims against UNI-PASS data, transport documents, and foreign exchange records. If the export documents are false, incomplete, or the proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory deadline, the supply is recategorized as taxable domestic supply, 10% VAT is assessed on the amount, input VAT refunds are clawed back with interest, and statutory surcharges apply. Deliberate fraudulent zero-rating can be prosecuted as tax evasion under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, leading to criminal fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK); foreign exchange administration is managed jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea has a flexible, OECD-aligned convertibility system with separate current and capital account disciplines. Current-account income, including EdTech subscriptions, Apple/Google app store proceeds, and software licensing fees, is freely convertible provided each inflow is credited to a licensed foreign exchange bank and tagged with a valid transaction code. Capital-account transactions, such as non-resident equity injection, shareholder loans, and treasury cross-border intercompany funding, require pre- or post-reporting, underlying contract evidence, and no anti-money laundering adverse findings. There is no required surrender of export proceeds to the central bank; firms may keep 100% of foreign currency in a foreign currency deposit. The chief remittance hurdle is documentary: profit repatriation requires proof of withholding tax settlement, audited or management accounts, a board resolution, and a capital transaction report for non-resident dividends, without which the bank will decline. Korea does not impose convertibility approval licences on ordinary registered corporations, but each transfer is subject to delegated bank surveillance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Bank of Korea operating notices, a resident exporter must receive service-export foreign exchange through a designated foreign exchange bank within 90 days of the service completion date, or within the contract payment terms if the underlying agreement and the foreign exchange bank approve a longer period. The mandatory surrender ratio is zero: no component of the export proceeds must be converted to KRW for central-bank reserves. The exporter may retain 100% in a foreign currency deposit account, but every receipt must be classified under the BOK Foreign Exchange Information System and reconciled with the platform settlement schedule. If the bank observes non-arrival within 90 days, it may suspend export tax and foreign-exchange privileges and require a formal explanation and documentary audit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not authorised as foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and are not licensed by the Financial Services Commission under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act; therefore they cannot legally hold a Korean corporate KRW current account, access KFTC clearing, issue foreign exchange transaction reports, or administer capital account compliance. Using an EMI for Korean operating income would circumvent reporting and create an AML red flag. Feasibility rating: Low; it should be used only as a supplementary payout collection tool for non-KR geographic sales where the Korean entity is not the legal creditor. The compliance path is to maintain first-line banking at a Korean Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors with signatory authority must attend a physical in-branch KYC interview at the time of account opening. Fully remote consular proxy opening is not permitted by Tier-1 Korean banks for a newly formed Chusik Hoesa. A non-resident director may delegate signing authority through a notarized power of attorney, but the authorized proxy must appear physically with the original POA, and the appointing director's identity is verified by passport and, where required, consular legalisation. In exceptional cases some banks accept apostille-style notarization for non-resident directors, but the local representative or a named officer with Korean registration card must be present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity in a private Chusik Hoesa share structure, especially non-resident shareholders with complex holding layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved and certified copy of the Korean corporate registry, full chronological share ledger, amended articles of incorporation, notarised UBO declaration listing each natural person with 25% or more ownership, organizational charts, passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners, and a board resolution attesting to the current ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: App store settlement masking: recurring Apple IAP and Google Play Billing transactions arrive as a single net settlement from foreign marketplace intermediaries, obscuring the origination of end-user funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple Developer Program and Google Play Developer agreements, monthly payout statements showing app purchase deduction breakdown, official sales dashboards, platform tax invoices, export service transaction list, and bank reconciliation explaining the net settlement amount and currency conversion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent economic substance for intangible EdTech services with no physical export documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business license, commercial office lease, payroll and social insurance records, technology licensing agreement, host and cloud service invoices, active user or automated tutorial session logs, product release notes, and audited financial statements demonstrating a marketable digital product.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound shareholder capital injection from a non-resident source where the source of wealth is not transparent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investor bank account reference, six months of account statements in the remitting entity or natural person, signed capital subscription agreement, foreign exchange report and certificate under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, source-of-wealth narrative, tax returns or provable salary, inheritance and investment documentation, and ultimate beneficial owner identification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder must remit cash to a temporary Foreign Investment Proceeds Escrow Account maintained at a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remittance wire must identify the payee company, the capital increase or share issuance purpose code, and the source of funds. Upon deposit and acceptance, the company files the Foreign Investment Report through the bank or the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency window; the bank then converts the remittance to KRW using the market offer rate, issues a Foreign Investment Report Certificate, and capital verification is performed by the company auditor based on the escrow deposit certificate, board resolution, and bank account statements. For a purely domestic Chusik Hoesa capital increase by a Korean shareholder, no FIPA report is needed, but each inward transfer must be reported by the bank as an inward remittance under the BOK transaction code. All cash injection routes must be non-anonymised and require prior bank approval for anti-money laundering release.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The company should route all treasury disbursements through SWIFT MT103 for ordinary operating costs, royalty, subscription, and intercompany payments; a Commercial Letter of Credit for high-value equipment, media, or content licences where a bank guarantee is required; and Documentary Collections for lightweight settlement of recurring intangible service invoices with buyer banks. Every outbound disbursement requires a supporting invoice or contract, a board resolution for large-ticket transfers, proper Korean withholding tax payment for foreign-deferred royalties and licensing fees, and a bank-confirmed transaction code matching the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act classification. Apple and Google platform disbursements from Korean app store accounts should be settled directly in KRW with the domestic bank rather than drawn on SWIFT rails unless the creditor is an offshore group company and the intercompany agreement is documented.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with licensed foreign exchange banks, tenor aligned to underlying export receivables and confirmed vendor invoices, notional capped at 110% of expected exposure.
Plain-vanilla FX options purchased by the Korean entity to protect USD/KRW revenue translation and procurement, with an upfront premium and no naked option writing.

Non-deliverable forward contracts approved by the bank treasury only for hedging non-KRW funding positions; NDFs are treated as risk-management instruments and cannot be used as standalone speculation.

Cross-currency swaps for matching USD/KRW project liabilities or invested capital, permitted as capital-account transactions when the economic purpose and source of repayment are documented to the foreign exchange bank, with no leveraged hybrid structures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders and approval of annual financial statements, profit appropriation, director reappointment, and statutory auditor appointment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None - internal corporate governance action; minutes retained at the registered office and made available to the National Tax Service and commercial registration court upon lawful demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to KRW 2,000,000 (approximately USD 1,500) may be imposed on each defaulting officer under the Korean Commercial Act; continued failure can trigger court inspection orders, director liability for loss, and loss of shareholder remedies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and audited or unaudited financial statements submitted with the tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the Hometax platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; calendar-year entity must file by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% of the underreported corporate tax, 40% for fraudulent or unfaithful returns, and 20% for ordinary non-filing; daily arrears interest accrues at 0.022% until full payment; persistent non-compliance can trigger enforced assessment, bank account seizure, and criminal prosecution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return (local surtax on national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: City, Gu, or County local tax office through the WetTax integrated local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same window as the national corporate income tax return; calendar-year entity must file by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local tax is subject to a surcharge of up to 3% of the unpaid amount, daily delinquency interest at 0.022%, and administrative collection measures including seizure of bank accounts and property

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Externally audited financial statements and independent auditor's report for companies meeting statutory audit thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Korea Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA); electronic disclosure through DART where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the annual shareholders' meeting; audited financial statements must be approved by 31 March and filed with FSS/KICPA within 15 days after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 37,000) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; FSS may appoint an auditor at the company's expense, the unaudited statements are rejected for disclosure and tax purposes, and directors face civil damages liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, if any foreign shareholder or foreign investment is present
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the reporting foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March following the fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within 90 days after that fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in a correction order, administrative fine up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700), and loss of foreign-investment protection and related tax subsidy benefits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit, shareholder register reconciliation, and internal UBO confirmation certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None - prepared for the board and statutory auditor and held at the registered office for NTS and court inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the annual shareholders' meeting and no later than 30 June after the fiscal year-end; share transfer registrations must be effected within 30 days of any transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are jointly and severally liable for loss caused by inaccurate or delayed register updates; each defaulting officer may be fined up to KRW 5,000,000 under the Korean Commercial Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent certified public accountant audit is required under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if, as of the fiscal year-end, the Chusik Hoesa meets any one of the following: (i) total assets equal to or exceeding KRW 12,000,000,000; (ii) total sales revenue for the fiscal year equal to or exceeding KRW 7,000,000,000; or (iii) average annual headcount of 300 or more employees. All listed companies and financial-industry companies are subject to external audit regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for listed companies, financial companies, and companies electing that framework; K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) for unlisted private Chusik Hoesa entities; audits must be performed in accordance with Korean Statements on Auditing Standards (KSA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation return for an ordinary private Chusik Hoesa. For a non-listed stock corporation, any share transfer is effective against the company only when recorded in the shareholder register; the transferee must apply for registration and the company must process the entry within 30 days of the transfer date. The register must show legal name, resident registration number or passport/foreigner ID, share class and number, transfer date, and consideration. For foreign-invested companies, beneficial ownership changes are confirmed by 31 March each year through the annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise Report to MOTIE or KOTRA. Failure to keep the register current may invalidate voting and dividend claims and triggers criminal and civil liability for directors.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors
Register of Charges/Mortgages and encumbrances on company assets
Minutes of Board of Directors' Meetings
Commercial accounting books, ledgers, and evidential vouchers
Register of Debentureholders, if bonds have been issued

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 3,600 per annum for a virtual/registered office plus basic corporate secretariat in Seoul; USD 8,000 to USD 18,000 for a full physical registered office with dedicated corporate support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 to USD 35,000 for a statutory certified audit of an unlisted EdTech Chusik Hoesa; USD 20,000 to USD 60,000 for a larger group with consolidated financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% maximum statutory corporate income tax rate before local surtax; progressive brackets: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200M, 19% on KRW 200M-20B, 21% on KRW 20B-300B, and 24% above KRW 300B. A 10% local income surtax is added to the CIT amount, making the effective top rate 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying technology-intensive firms, including EdTech and language-learning software companies, may claim: (i) R&D expense tax credits of up to 25% for SMEs under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; (ii) Korean Free Economic Zone / foreign-invested zone holidays: 100% corporate income tax exemption for the first 3 years and 50% reduction for the next 2 years; (iii) patent-box-like deduction for income from qualifying copyrighted software, user-generated content analytics, and technology licensing under applicable IP provisions of the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; and (iv) investment tax credits for high-tech facility acquisition.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Return filed electronically through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with semi-annual prepayment installments for corporations having prior-year taxable income)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months of the close of the fiscal year (i.e., 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year-end). Provisional semi-annual returns are due within 2 months after the first six months of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates the start and end dates of the legal fiscal year and the entity status as a domestic company (Chusik Hoesa, resident Korea entity).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an entity established by a non-resident parent, verify that the Korean filing year is not conflated with the foreign parent's fiscal year and disclose any short-period return due to newly-incorporating or opening of a PE. All foreign ownership and place-of-effective-management details must be footnoted for NTS audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Total revenue (subscription and app-store transactions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Korean-sourced subscription revenue from Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, direct B2B licensing, and language-learning tutoring software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross receipts before Apple/Google commission deduction. Revenue attributable to non-resident users must be segregated if an overseas server or foreign PE exists. Failure to separate export revenue from local revenue will distort the territorial source test and may trigger transfer pricing review at the transaction level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Taxable income after adjustments and carried-forward losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Korean taxable income after cost deductions, roll-over adjustments, R&D credits, and available NOL carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If any non-resident staff or licensor receives royalty for the EdTech platform, deductions are allowed only if the payment is arm's length, properly withheld, and supported by functional and entity substance. Enter positive numbers without direction; any loss claimed must use the statutory 10-year carryforward and be documented with the revenue agency schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 16 - Corporate tax calculation at progressive brackets and surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of base CIT and 10% local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and controlling foreign corporations should ensure that any Korean PE profits are brought into the same computation. The local surtax is an additional requirement for any foreign parent's tax credit planning; retain source documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 24 - Foreign tax credit / income tax withheld facts and DTA relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule for foreign taxes paid by the Korean entity and/or withholding tax credits arising from non-resident dividends, interest, and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For treaty rate application, the foreign recipient must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its tax authority within the preceding 12 months, a beneficial ownership statement, and proof of substantive operations. Any credit taken must be reconciled to actual tax paid, and the NTS will deny credits if the transaction is a shell-company arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 31 - Non-resident payments (dividends, interest, royalties, services)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of outbound payments to foreign shareholders or affiliates, including gross amount, identity, legal address, country, and withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border dividend WHT is statutorily 22%; interest and royalty are also 22%. Treaty-reduced rates may be applied only after a valid treaty relief application is processed. For EdTech royalty payments to the parent, add transfer pricing schedules and economic substance evidence; otherwise the NTS can recharacterize and impose high non-resident penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing penalty: 20% of the unpaid tax under Article 47-2 of the Corporate Income Tax Act. Underreporting penalty: 10% of the omitted tax; fraudulent underreporting: 40% under Article 47-3. Unpaid tax accrues daily interest at 0.022% under Article 47-14. Failure to withhold non-resident tax triggers a 20% withholding-related penalty plus personal collection from the responsible representative. Criminal tax fraud thresholds under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act apply for deliberate false declarations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory outbound dividend withholding tax (20% national tax plus 10% resident surtax on that 20%). Certain tax treaties reduce to 5%-15% depending on shareholding and parent-subsidiary tests.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident must: (i) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence for the relevant income period; (ii) complete a Korean Application for Withholding Tax Exemption or Reduction together with a beneficial ownership declaration and, where a royalty, interest, or service payment, a business substance certificate confirming the non-resident is the true economic owner and performs Core Income-Generating Activities; (iii) submit the documentation to the Korean payor or withholding agent before the payment due date; and (iv) file the monthly withholding return and pay the applicable treaty rate. If the treaty benefit is challenged, the NTS can require a refund claim or reassessment. A TRC alone is not enough; the OECD MLI principal purpose test and Korean substance rules apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on outbound royalties and interest is 22% (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Under most Korean DTAs, royalties on copyrighted computer programs and software are reduced to 0%-10% (typically 10% or 2%-5% for industrial or commercial royalties), and interest to 5%-10%. The 22% rate applies unless a valid treaty relief certificate is in hand at the time of payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory preparation of Master File and Local File; consolidated group revenue of KRW 100 billion triggers Country-by-Country report filing. For smaller EdTech firms, the NTS still may issue transfer pricing documentation summons under OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Korea has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations, the substance-over-form principle (Article 10, Framework Act on National Taxes), OECD MLI PPT provisions, and domestic CFC rules apply. For a Chusik Hoesa in EdTech, substance is tested through actual mobile-payment operation, content and local tutoring function, software development staff, and management decisions in Korea. If non-resident ownership creates a conduit arrangement, the Korean entity's revenue may be recharacterized as a PE of the foreign parent, leading to disallowance of royalties, WHT enforcement, and severe tax penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting app-store and Apple/Google Billing revenue from the Korean corporate return, creating shell invoices for algorithm development at a foreign related party, and fabricating R&D tax credit expenses in the language-learning software.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 47-2 and 47-3 of the Corporate Income Tax Act impose negligence surcharges of 20% for non-filing and 10%-40% for underreporting. Under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, criminal tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment of up to 2 years, or up to 3 years where evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million, and a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director(s) may be jointly and severally liable for the entity's unpaid tax, surcharge, and interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes; the NTS may order deposit of personal assets, suspend departure (travel ban / blacklisting), and impose civil restitution orders. If fraud is proven in a criminal trial, the director faces imprisonment and permanent barring from serving on corporations in Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold non-resident tax / DTA relief misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident parent without withholding 22% tax, or using an invalid foreign TRC to pay at a treaty-reduced rate without actual beneficial ownership, e.g., using a shell holding company covering the Korean entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is personally liable for the amount not withheld and for the 20% additional charge under Article 47-2 of the Corporate Income Tax Act. If a treaty rate is improperly applied, the NTS imposes a 40% unfair underreporting addition, plus daily unpaid-delay interest at 0.022%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally approved the payment are civilly liable for the unremitted WHT and additions. In serious cases, the violation constitutes criminal tax fraud, leading to imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine of up to 5 times the withheld amount. The NTS may blacklist the company and director to prevent overseas travel and may initiate seizure of personal accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Korean Chusik Hoesa with no staff, no Korean office, no business records beyond App Store identity, and no local decision-making, while substantial profits are stripped out as royalties or trademark fees to a low-tax holding company as part of an EdTech group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The GAAR under Article 10 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 62 CFC rules allow the NTS to recharacterize the Korean entity as a permanent establishment of the foreign parent, deny royalty and interest deductions, and impose a 40% unfair underreporting addition and a 20% withholding violation charge. Treaty relief is denied under the MLI principal purpose test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil of the Chusik Hoesa and render directors personally liable for the corporate tax assessed, including asset restitution and compensation for losses. Directors also face criminal charges of fraud or tax evasion, travel restrictions, and possible imprisonment where cross-border asset hiding is shown; the company's foreign parent may also be required to register a Korean PE and retroactively withhold all non-resident payments.
